title: Sigstore-backed residency signing and immutable proof export for Dedicated tenants
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a Sigstore-compatible signing workflow and immutable export package for Dedicated tenant residency proofs. The service will collect deterministic residency signals from Dedicated node agents (region, host UUID, VM/container fingerprint, kernel time-window, attached storage metadata), produce a canonical residency manifest, sign the manifest using a customer- or Redwood-managed key via KMS/HSM, and publish an immutable, verifiable proof bundle (manifest + signature + provenance metadata) that customers and auditors can fetch or receive via webhook. The goal is to provide cryptographically verifiable evidence of tenant-bound residency and isolation without leaking tenant data, and to make exports replay-proof and tamper-evident.
scope: Collect node-level residency signals from Dedicated runtime agents
Canonicalize and version residency manifests per tenant per day (and ad-hoc on-demand)
Integrate Sigstore-style transparency and signing flow using Redwood KMS or customer KMS (via HSM-backed signing when available)
Export signed, compressed proof bundles (ZIP/PAR2) with manifest, signature, certificate chain, and runtime provenance
Provide API endpoints and console UI for scheduled exports and on-demand retrieval
Retention controls to redact transient identifiers and enforce configurable retention windows
out_of_scope: Full tenant data snapshots or any plaintext customer data in bundles
Real-time streaming of proofs to auditors (only scheduled/export-on-demand initially)
acceptance_criteria: Residency agent successfully emits canonical signals once per hour from 90% of Dedicated nodes in canary region
Service can build a signed manifest and return a downloadable bundle via API (signed with Redwood-managed KMS key)
Signed bundles include certificate chain and verification instructions and validate using standard Sigstore tooling
Exported bundles redact PII/tenant data per retention rules and include a redaction report
Automated CI test covers signature verification and tamper-detection for example bundles
Operational runbook exists for key rotation and emergency revocation, and security review completed
design_decisions: Use Sigstore-compatible signature format to maximize third-party verifier tool compatibility
Canonical manifest schema will be JSON-LD to enable stable canonicalization across languages
By default sign with Redwood KMS; allow opt-in customer KMS for Dedicated Enterprise tenants
Store short-lived proof artifacts in immutable object store with content-addressable IDs (CAS) and export a signed reference to the CAS object
Retention/redaction implemented at manifest build-time rather than post-export to prevent sensitive fields from entering storage
tradeoffs: Using Sigstore format increases interoperability but adds dependency on external verification norms
Customer-managed KMS adds complexity (rotation/process) but is required for enterprise compliance
Canonicalization (JSON-LD) is more complex to implement but reduces verifier ambiguity across languages
Storing signed bundles in CAS increases storage cost but simplifies tamper-evidence and deduplication
implementation_tasks: Agent: add residency signal collector to dedicated-node agent (node metadata, instance id, vpc-id, region, timestamp, kernel fingerprint)
API: residency-manifest-builder service to collect signals, canonicalize, and assemble manifest
Security: KMS integration layer for Redwood and customer KMS; sign manifests using HSM when available
Storage: implement CAS-backed immutable bucket and retention lifecycle policies
Export: bundle generator that packages manifest + signature + certs + provenance + redaction report
Console: UI for scheduling exports, viewing previous bundles, and initiating on-demand export
CI/tests: add unit/integration tests to verify signature and canonicalization across Node/Rust/Python verifiers
Runbook: key rotation, emergency revoke, and auditor access procedures
tests_and_validation: Unit: canonicalization tests with representative manifests across languages
Integration: end-to-end bundle creation and Sigstore verification in staging
Load: generate bundles for 100 tenants concurrently to verify manifest builder throughput
Security: threat model review and pen test of signing endpoints
Compliance: internal audit checklist mapping export artifacts to SOC2/GDPR requirements
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: build canary residency-agent and staging manifest builder; manual verification of bundles
Week 3: enable scheduled nightly exports for internal test tenants and run verification jobs
Week 4-5: opt-in beta for 3 pilot Dedicated tenants with customer KMS option; collect feedback
Week 6: full Dedicated rollout in non-EU regions; EU and APAC rollout gated on legal review
Post-release: telemetry dashboard for proof generation success rate and signer latency; iterate
monitoring_and_alerting: SLOs: 99.9% manifest build success over 24h for production tenants
Alerts: signer error spike, KMS auth failures, CAS write errors, high redaction-rate anomalies
security_considerations: Limit manifest contents to non-sensitive residency signals; do not include raw tenant payloads
Key usage audited and logged; signing keys stored in HSM for Redwood-managed keys
Customer KMS flows will be strictly separated and only used with customer consent and documented key policies
All APIs require mTLS + token auth; console exports audited with user and action context
notes_and_followups: Follow-up ticket to add cross-cloud federation (ENG-42177 suggested)
Coordinate legal for export-of-records policy for EU customers before EU rollout
Add a small SDK verifier for auditors in Go and Python to simplify customer verification
Consider adding transparency log (Sigstore Rekor) post-beta to increase public auditability
